title: Does Leaving the Fridge Open Cool the Room? No.
caption: Your fridge doesn't make cold. It moves heat out of the box, which is why an open fridge warms your kitchen.
pinned_comment: Did you know an open fridge heats your kitchen? Yes or no 👇

lines.text: Your fridge is secretly a heater.
Leave the door open on a hot day, and your kitchen gets warmer, not cooler.
Here's why. A fridge doesn't make cold. It moves heat.
A liquid called refrigerant flows through a sealed loop of pipes.
Inside the walls, it boils into a gas, far below freezing.
Boiling soaks up heat, so the warmth from your food flows into it.
Then a compressor squeezes that gas until it's hotter than your kitchen.
Coils on the back dump that heat into the room. Feel the back of your fridge. It's warm.
That warmth is the heat that just left your food.
The gas cools, turns back into a liquid, and the loop starts again.
With the door open, the fridge just moves kitchen heat in a circle.

visual.title: Open fridge on a hot day

lines.text: And its motor adds even more heat on top.
So when someone yells, close the fridge, you're letting the cold out, it's the other way around. Because…
